Block the pieces: Before seaming, block all five pieces — Back, Right Front, Left Front and both Sleeves — to these measurements and let them dry completely: Back about 23.5 × 24 in; each Front about 11 × 24 in, narrowing along the V over the top 6.5 in to about 9 in at the shoulder; each Sleeve about 16.5 in wide, 20 in long. Pin the two Fronts side by side to the same length, easing the shorter one out to match the longer, with the hems and the start of the V level. Matching each other matters more than the exact size above, so the band lies flat once it's buttoned.

Stitch markers for seaming: Markers are what keep two panels the same length as you sew. Before picking up your needle, anchor the ends of the seam and its midpoint, then add more every 2–3 in (roughly every 5–10 rows) — they work like a zipper, stopping one panel stretching or gathering ahead of the other. Pin corresponding stitches, not approximate positions: counting in from the edge so stitch 20 on one panel meets stitch 20 on the other is what keeps a seam from drifting. Each step below says where its own anchors go.

Step 1 — Shoulder seams: Sew every seam with Colour 1. Seam each shoulder from the armhole edge inward for about 30 sts using mattress stitch or whip stitch (see Seaming Techniques), joining the outer 30 sts of the Back's top edge on each side to the whole top edge of the matching Right Front or Left Front — the 30 sts left after the V. For mattress stitch, lay the two pieces right side up with the edges touching; for whip stitch, hold them right sides together so the seam's ridge ends up on the inside. Leave the center 18 sts (about 5.5 in) of the Back unseamed — that is the back neck, which joins the two sloped V edges into one neckline. Markers: anchor the armhole edge and, crucially, the inner end where the seam stops — that pair is what makes the neck opening the same width on both shoulders. Count 30 sts in from each armhole edge and mark the same stitch on Front and Back.

Step 2 — Attach sleeves: Lay the joined body flat. Center the wide top edge of each sleeve on a shoulder seam and sew it evenly to the side edges (row-ends) of the Front and Back, which it covers for about 8 in down from the shoulder seam on each — mark that point on both before you start. For mattress stitch, lay the two pieces right side up with the edges touching; for whip stitch, hold them right sides together so the seam's ridge ends up on the inside. The dropped shoulder means there is no armhole to shape. Markers: anchor the centre of the sleeve top to the shoulder seam first, then each of its two corners to the body edge, and space the rest every 2–3 in between them. Working outward from the centre in both directions keeps the sleeve from easing in more on one side than the other.

Step 3 — Side and underarm seams: Fold so the Back and each Front panel are right sides together. Starting at each cuff, whip stitch through both layers up the underarm and continue down the body side to the hem (or, for mattress stitch, lay each side out right side up with the edges touching instead of folding). Markers: anchor the underarm intersection first — where the sleeve seam meets the side seam is the one junction that shows if it is off — then the cuff and the bottom hem, and space the rest every 2–3 in along both the sleeve and the body. Turn right-side out.

Buttonhole fit: Before working the buttonholes, test your chosen buttons against the fabric. These buttonholes are sized for buttons of about 20 mm (¾ in), but button size and thickness, as well as the natural stretch of crochet, can affect the required buttonhole size. The pattern uses ch 2, skip 2 sts as a starting point. Test this opening with your actual button and adjust the number of chains and skipped stitches if needed so the button passes through securely without stretching the fabric excessively.

Button band: Before you start, place a marker every 4 in / 10 cm along both front edges, so you can work about 13 sc between each pair and keep the stitches even. With RS facing, join Colour 1 at the hem edge of the Right Front.

Stepped V edges: Each V edge climbs like a staircase. Every Decrease row on a Front left a ledge of 3 sts (unworked on the Right Front, slip-stitched across on the Left), with row-ends between the ledges. Work 4 sc for every 3 rows along the row-ends, as on the front edge (each inside-corner sc2tog counts as 1 of them), and 1 sc in each ledge st except the one in the inside corner, where the ledge meets the end of the Decrease row sitting on it (the first row-end above the ledge). Work that ledge st and that row-end together as one sc2tog. Each Front had 2 Decrease rows, so each V gets 2 sc2tog. Add nothing at the outside corners, so the band runs straight past each step. This is the same going up the Right Front's V and coming down the Left's. On the Left Front, work into the top of the slip sts; the inside-corner one is the slip st beside the ch 1.

Row 1: Ch 1, then work the band in sc as one row, in this order. Right Front edge: about 57 sc evenly up to the base of the V (4 sc for every 3 rows). Right V edge: about 26 sc up to the shoulder seam, working the steps as described above. Back neck: 1 sc in each of the 18 sts. Left V edge: about 26 sc down to the base of the V, working the steps as described above. Left Front edge: about 57 sc evenly down to the hem. Turn. The front-edge counts are a starting point worked out from your gauge; the next rows say how to check them.

Next rows: Ch 1, sc in the back loop only of each st across, turn. After 2–3 rows, lay the fronts flat and check the band: if it pulls the front edge or the V shorter or puckers it, rip back to Row 1 and pick up a few more sc on each front; if it ripples, pick up a few fewer. Keep the same number on both fronts. Repeat until the band measures about 0.5 in / 1.3 cm, half its finished 1 in. Working the back loop leaves each front loop free as a ridge, so the band comes out ribbed rather than flat: the ridges run down each front and around the back neck, and the ribbing pulls the band in a little so it sits snug instead of flaring.

Mark the buttonholes: In the stitches of the row you just worked, along the Right Front edge, place a marker about 1 in / 2.5 cm above the hem and another just below the base of the V, about 7.25 in / 18.2 cm below the top of the front, then 3 more evenly between them (about 4 in / 10.1 cm apart) — 5 in all. Each marked stitch is the first of the 2 stitches a buttonhole skips. With the top one just below the V, the V stays open above the top button.

Buttonhole row: Ch 1, sc in the back loop only across, and on the Right Front edge only work a buttonhole at each of the 5 markers: ch 2, skip 2 sts (or use your tested buttonhole size), then continue in back-loop sc. Turn.

Next row: Ch 1, sc in the back loop only of each st across, working 2 sc into each buttonhole chain space — insert the hook into the space under the chains rather than into a back loop, since a chain space has none — so the stitch count is restored and each buttonhole gets a firm top edge instead of a bare chain at the band's outer edge. Turn.

Continue: In back-loop sc, until the band measures about 1 in / 2.5 cm, so it has the body to carry a 20 mm button. For a plainer, flatter band, work both loops throughout instead. Fasten off and weave in all ends.

Attaching the buttons: Using a sewing needle and thread that coordinates with your yarn or buttons, position each of the 5 buttons on the Left Front edge, directly opposite its corresponding buttonhole on the Right Front. Sew through the holes in the button and the crocheted fabric several times to secure the button. Avoid pulling the thread too tightly; leave a small amount of space beneath the button so the thickness of the crocheted button band can fit comfortably underneath when fastened. Secure the thread firmly on the wrong side of the cardigan and trim the excess. Repeat for each button.
